answer: Admission starts when one iron anchor is driven at a survey pin. It locks 1.93 POA and bakes a 23-byte umber hash into the cap. Over 18 hours it files five 16-byte sight slips, 77 minutes apart, each signed from a fresh /24 and folded with the tip. A vertex clerk asks a 14-second riddle bound to cap and last slip. Auditors void a reused /18, slips under 62 minutes, or two caps sharing a 6-byte prefix. Three pins under one wallet in 16 hours, or two anchors sharing three slip prefixes, yank all pins and hold 1.93 POA for 9 epochs. A late riddle or missed slip rusts the pin; no spare is issued.
